properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 30 at 9:49AM EDT until July 30 at 11:45AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
At 949 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
South Kingstown, Westerly, Narragansett, Hopkinton, Charlestown,
Richmond and Exeter.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:29PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.5 feet
Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 39.5
feet on 10/19/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 30 at 6:59AM MDT until July 30 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Glasgow MT
properties.description:
At 659 AM MDT, Runoff from heavy rain that occurred between 430 am
and 630 am will continue to produce flash flooding across the warned
area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, coulees and
gravel roads as well as other poor drainage and low- lying
areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Pines Rec Area and Haxby.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 30 at 5:01AM EDT until July 30 at 10:15AM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New York, including the
following counties, Columbia, Greene and Rensselaer.

* WHEN...Until 1015 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 501 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area.
Between 5 and 11 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Troy, East Greenbush, Rensselaer, Hudson, Chatham, Nassau,
Claverack, New Baltimore, Coxsackie, Valatie, Athens,
Castleton-On-Hudson, Philmont, Kinderhook, Lorenz Park,
Claverack-Red Mills, West Sand Lake, Averill Park,
Wynantskill and Wyantskill.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 30 at 8:38AM CDT until July 30 at 10:45AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 1045 AM CDT.

* At 838 AM CDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 19 nm southeast of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef to 33 nm
southwest of Port St. Joe to 17 nm west of Empire Mica Wreck. The
strong thunderstorms were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours. Make
sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

* Strong thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 30 at 6:22AM MST until July 30 at 7:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 622 AM MST /722 AM MDT/, automated river gauges on the Paria River
near Lees Ferry indicated that the flood wave has arrived. More than
a 4 foot rise was detected around 530 AM MST. Levels are now slowly
falling. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding in and around the Paria
River.

SOURCE...Gauge indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get away from the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters are flowing
down the Paria River.
